title: Making Upside Down’s AI cover communicate Anunnaki mythology and impossible gravity
author: goyasapiens
selftext:
I'm the developer of Upside Down, a Three.js browser puzzle game built around Anunnaki mythology and quantum-inspired ideas. You play a winged guardian in a floating Mesopotamian temple and choose which way gravity pulls.



I used image generation to develop the launch artwork. Getting the model to show the mechanic was the difficult part. Asking for a character standing sideways on a wall kept producing an upright character stuck to the wall. Specifying the contact points and screen-space orientation made the instruction much clearer: both soles on the wall, feet at the left, head at the right, with the body horizontal relative to the upright palms.



The wordmark had a similar problem. Rotating a whole word 180 degrees also reverses its letter order. The approved mark flips UPSIDE top-to-bottom while keeping its letters in order. Explicitly describing the downward-open U and lower bowl of the P helped the model get there.



The cinematic cover shifts the emphasis to a guardian looking out toward the temple. I added the website and generated the QR code separately, then checked that the exported QR decodes to the correct URL. The attached image is AI-generated promotional art.



The first 26 rooms are playable free: [https://tryupsidedown.com/play/index.html](https://tryupsidedown.com/play/index.html)
